findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource and no ACL is set on this bucket, so it relies entirely on account/provider defaults for public access protection.
The bucket stores sensitive financial ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so operational runbook data is stored unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL. This appears to be a typo for 'log-delivery-write', and an invalid value could cause apply-time failure or unexpected access behavior on a bucket that stores sensitive audit logs.
The object is uploaded into reports_archive, a bucket with no server-side encryption configured, so this vendor roster file is stored in cleartext at rest.

force_destroy = true is set on a bucket holding reports data without any compensating access controls (no encryption, no ACL, no public access block), increasing the risk that data can be irrecoverably deleted alongside its other exposures.
